question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose the exec denylist in both openclaw.json and exec-approvals.json with unioned deny-over-allow behavior across gateway, node, and macOS companion hosts?
rationale: This is a new fail-closed execution security policy with two persisted operator surfaces; implementation review cannot determine the intended long-term ownership, UX, and upgrade contract.

options.title: Choose one canonical owner
options.body: Keep the denylist in one persisted policy surface and remove the parallel authoring path before merge.

options.title: Accept both surfaces
options.body: Approve the unioned dual-surface contract and require merged-head native proof plus explicit operator documentation.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Pause or close this implementation if the cross-runtime and dual-policy complexity is not worth the capability.

recommendation.title: Choose one canonical owner
recommendation.body: Keep the denylist in one persisted policy surface and remove the parallel authoring path before merge.
